questions.question: What is the main purpose of taking notes while reading or listening?
choices: Capture useful ideas in a form that supports later understanding or work
Copy every word without selecting information

questions.question: Which note is most useful for distinguishing a source's claim from its evidence?
choices: Claim: school gardens improve access; evidence: harvest records from three years

questions.question: A student copies a paragraph into notes without quotation marks or a citation. What is the risk?
choices: The notes will become too concise
The source will be easier to verify
The copied language may later be mistaken for the student's own writing
The main idea will be stated more clearly

questions.question: Which organizer is best for comparing two proposed solutions across cost, time, and impact?
A student researches a question and wants notes to preserve where each fact came from. What should be recorded alongside the note?
choices: Source details or a citation key
The number of paragraphs in the source

questions.question: Which note-taking method best supports a later summary?
choices: Group key ideas by topic and record concise supporting details
Write isolated keywords with no context

questions.question: A concept map places 'erosion' at the center and links causes, effects, and examples. What does this structure show well?
When is a timeline organizer most appropriate?
choices: When comparing the reliability of websites
When the order and timing of events matter

questions.question: A student uses Cornell notes. What belongs in the cue column?
choices: Questions or key terms that help prompt recall of the notes
A full copy of every source page
Decorative images unrelated to the lesson
A second copy of the title only

questions.question: What is a useful reason to paraphrase a source in notes?
choices: It removes the need to cite the source
It checks understanding and separates the student's wording from the source's wording
It guarantees the source is accurate

questions.question: A source gives a statistic but not the date or population measured. What should the note-taker do?
choices: Mark the missing context and seek it before relying on the statistic

questions.question: Which organizer helps sort evidence into reasons for and against a claim?
A student has notes from five sources. How can they reduce accidental overreliance on one source?
choices: Track which ideas come from each source and compare evidence across them
Combine all wording into one paragraph

questions.question: Why should notes use labels or headings?
choices: They prove the ideas are correct
They make ideas easier to locate and synthesize later
They remove the need for supporting details

questions.question: Which note is clearest and most useful?
choices: Flood risk rose after wetlands were drained; county map shows affected zones

questions.question: What is the strongest reason to revise notes after a research session?
choices: Turn every note into a quotation
Clarify shorthand, group related ideas, and identify unanswered questions

questions.question: A Venn diagram is most useful for
choices: showing shared and distinct features of two or more subjects

questions.question: A student copies a quotation into notes for possible use. What should be included immediately?
choices: A paraphrase that hides the original wording
Quotation marks and enough source information to locate it
A new title for the quotation

questions.question: A research organizer has columns for claim, evidence, source, and limitation. What does the limitation column encourage?
choices: Evaluation of what the evidence can and cannot establish

questions.question: Which action best turns notes into a synthesis?
choices: Paste notes in the order they were collected
List source titles without explaining them
Connect ideas across sources and explain how they answer the research question
